title: けど ／ けれども
meaning: "but / although" — casual equivalent of the conjunction が.
simpleExplanation: けど means "but / although" and is the casual version of the conjunction が. 高いけど、買います "It's expensive, but I'll buy it". It attaches to plain or polite forms. Nouns and な-adjectives take だけど in plain style (学生だけど). From casual to formal: けど < けれど < けれども. At the end of a sentence, 〜けど… leaves the thought hanging politely.
whenUsed: Everyday conversation with friends and family. In polite conversation, けど after ですます is common and acceptable; in writing, が is preferred.
formation: Clause 1 (plain or polite) + けど／けれど／けれども、Clause 2

examples.en: It's expensive, but I'll buy it.

examples.ja: 頑張ったけど、試験に落ちました。
examples.reading: がんばったけど、しけんに おちました。
examples.en: I tried hard, but I failed the exam.

examples.ja: 田中さんは親切だけど、ちょっと厳しいです。
examples.reading: たなかさんは しんせつだけど、ちょっと きびしいです。
examples.en: Mr Tanaka is kind, but a little strict.

examples.ja: この店は有名だけど、ちょっと高い。
examples.reading: この みせは ゆうめいだけど、ちょっと たかい。
examples.en: This shop is famous, but a bit expensive.

examples.ja: 雨が降っているけど、出かけます。
examples.reading: あめが ふっているけど、でかけます。
examples.en: It's raining, but I'm going out.
examples.note: Plain verb + けど, polite ending.

similarGrammar.difference: Same meaning; が is more polite and used in writing.
でも begins a new sentence.

commonMistakes.why: Nouns need だ before けど in plain style.
な-adjectives need だ before けど.

usageNotes: な-adjectives and nouns take だけど in plain style (親切だけど, 学生だけど). Politeness scale: けど (casual) < けれど < けれども (formal) ≈ が. At the end of a sentence 〜けど… leaves the thought trailing politely.
jlptTips: Blank between a noun/な-adjective and けど → だ. After an い-adjective or verb → nothing.
The exam often tests けど against から: contrast vs reason.
